svg.title: S3 Object Lock: what protects a version
svg.desc: An object version in a bucket with Object Lock and versioning can carry a retention period with a retain-until-date in governance or compliance mode, and independently a legal hold. Governance: delete, overwrite, shorten or remove only by principals with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention who send the x-amz-bypass-governance-retention header; the console sends it automatically. Compliance: nobody, including the root user, can delete, overwrite, shorten or change the mode until the date; it can only be extended; the only way out earlier is closing the account. Legal hold: no date, blocks deletion in both modes until someone with s3:PutObjectLegalHold removes it, and the governance bypass does not override it. All of them apply immediately, with no grace period.
svg.text: S3 Object Lock: what protects a version
Versioning on · each version has its own lock · new versions and delete markers are still allowed
sec/trade-log.csv · version 5f00cebe...
ObjectLockMode · ObjectLockRetainUntilDate · ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus · ObjectLockEventHold
RETENTION: GOVERNANCE
Locked for most users
Delete, overwrite, shorten, remove or change mode:
only with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention
+ x-amz-bypass-governance-retention: true
The console sends the header for you.
Extend: anyone with s3:PutObjectRetention.
Use it to test settings and against accidents.
RETENTION: COMPLIANCE
Locked for everybody, root user included
No delete, overwrite, shortening or mode change
until the retain-until-date. The bypass flag
changes nothing.
Extend only: a later retain-until-date.
Only way out earlier: close the AWS account.
Use it for SEC 17a-4, CFTC, FINRA records.
LEGAL HOLD (INDEPENDENT, BOTH MODES)
No date: blocks delete and overwrite until someone with s3:PutObjectLegalHold sets it OFF. The governance bypass does not override it.
All of these apply immediately. There is no grace or cooling-off period in S3 Object Lock (that is AWS Backup Vault Lock).
